item: A confirmed-damaged library file is repaired at start-up by a salvage copy and a switch, and the kept damaged file is removed 30 days later (E3, R121, R129)
key_paths: src/database/salvage.py; src/database/repair.py; src/database/damage.py; src/api/boot_sequence.py; src/api/main.py; src/api/jobs.py; src/database/verify.py; src/database/library_generation.py; src/backup/merge.py; src/database/session.py; src/static/app-core.js; src/static/taskmanager.js; tests/test_salvage.py; tests/test_repair.py; tests/test_repair_kept_copy.py; tests/test_library_generation.py; tests/damaged_store_helpers.py; tests/living_sources_node_test.js
summary: When the start-up check (E2) read a table of the corpus file as damaged in this process, the boot step repair-database (after verify-database, before article-indexes, while the app is offline) copies every row it can still read into a new file: ids are probed one at a time past unreadable pages, a failure that is not corruption aborts the copy instead of dropping the row, children of an unreadable parent are kept and counted, AUTOINCREMENT counters never fall below a lost id, the copy has the damaged file's own page size and encryption and the passphrase is in no record. The copy is rebuilt (indexes, search index), checked with the start-up's own per-table read and switched in under the write gate and the exclusive window: the damaged file gets a second name by a hard link (<stem>.damaged-<UTC>), the live log is removed so it can never be replayed into the new file, os.replace puts the copy under the live name; a power cut between the steps is resumed (only by a start that measured the damage itself, R100), finished (a cut right after the replace: the record, the corpus epoch and the follow-up steps are made at the next start) or discarded at the next start by the damaged file's identity, which includes the size of the log because in WAL mode a commit leaves the main file's size, time and inode alone; the swap folds the log into the file first and compares the identity again after the fold. A connection a request had checked out before the replace is refused its next statement, COMMIT or checkout (src/database/library_generation.py: a stamp per connection taken before the file is opened under a lock the swap holds exclusively, and a counter the swap bumps FIRST), so a save that waited out the repair fails loudly instead of committing into the kept file; the repair and the restore move the name through ONE helper and ONE window (swap_in_corpus in src/backup/merge.py), the repair's last check inside it is a data-version read on a connection held open since the copy began (any save by any path refuses the switch and the copy is made again at the next start), and the repair declines when the write gate is switched off, which now also gates text() writes on a corpus session. A sidecar is an untrusted input: every name and the identity it carries are checked, only a sidecar that fails is removed, never a file it names, and scratch goes only by its whole name. The copy and the folders are fsynced. Nothing the copy read is removed: where a table without AUTOINCREMENT would hand a lost tail id to the next row, which would then seem to own the children kept for it, an AUTOINCREMENT parent's counter is raised, a key declared ON DELETE SET NULL is set to NULL, and any other parent gets one stand-in row marked (lost <table> <id>) at the highest id its children refer to (counted per table, tables with measured verdicts named, a refused stand-in named as id reuse possible); the children of a gap are kept. Refusals are named and leave every file as it was (schema unreadable, no hard links, not enough free space, two unfinished starts in a row, writer busy). R129 (answer 35 = b): the kept damaged file is removed 30 days after the repaired file first read clean, at a start only, never while a repair or a check runs or the library is latched damaged again, only the file the repair recorded (name pattern, folder, inode, a plain file, not a link) with its -wal link, the removal (date, bytes) recorded in the repair record, and the notice and the Diagnostics zip say its size, where it is and the removal date in all twelve languages. OO_BOOT_REPAIR=0 switches the repair and the removal off. A copy in which a read FAILED AT THE DISK (the repair's raw read of the damaged file, where a short read counts as unread, or the start-up check's own unread pages) is kept and never removed after 30 days: no date is recorded and the notice says the drive could not read N pages and to check the drive; with OO_BOOT_REPAIR=0 the notice says the removal is off. Not repaired: the Wikipedia and law files, a finding this process did not measure; a file damaged while the app runs is checked at the next start and repaired then if the check confirms it.
